<!-- Modified by lavinhoque33, 2026-11-11. -->
## Dev build

This is a prerelease, not a regular release. It is not served as "latest", and the regular build stays on v1.33.0. The dev build contains YouTube and YouTube Music. Installing a dev module replaces the regular module of the same app, and the next regular build is then offered as an update.

## New in dev.7

- **Download quality:** Miscellaneous > Downloads now has one quality setting for future individual song, playlist and album downloads: Highest (default), High, Normal or Low. It applies to both Stream download and Device files, is captured once per download or batch, and is disabled for YouTube Music / external app. Existing copies stay unchanged; changing quality does not redownload or transcode them.
- **Source quality tiers:** Highest prefers the highest source actually offered, including AAC 141 or Opus 774 at about 256 kbps when available, then the standard tiers. High prefers standard Opus 251; Normal prefers AAC 140 at about 128 kbps; Low prefers HE-AAC 139 at about 48 kbps or Opus 249 at about 50 kbps. When a tier is unavailable, the nearest available source is used. Codec tiers, not variable-bitrate byte counts, determine quality. This does not unlock Premium formats or create higher-quality audio by transcoding.
- **Saved playback:** Each new stream copy keeps its original codec and stream identity for online and offline playback. Online, the local copy still works with lyrics and radio. Cached AAC was tested after an online session and from a fully offline cold start, including middle-of-song seeks. Matched 360p video copies keep the selected-quality audio, with local playback and seeking in both Song and Video modes.
- **Android Auto verification:** In Song mode, the Desktop Head Unit displayed downloaded artwork, played saved AAC 140 and advanced with its real Next button to an existing saved Opus 251 track in the correct queue. An explicit Video selection can still stream its online video; this does not force it back to Song mode.

## Included from dev.6

- **One Download method:** YouTube Music now uses one setting for songs, playlists and albums: Stream download (default), Device files, or YouTube Music / external app. Stream download saves a private copy for playback online and offline. Device files saves files in the device library. The last method uses Music or an external downloader; external overrides apply to individual songs, while playlists and albums stay with Music. A download never writes both a device file and a stream copy. Earlier settings migrate to Stream first, then Device files, and changing the method never deletes existing downloads. Download settings are grouped under Miscellaneous > Downloads.
- **Individual stream downloads:** Download a song from its menu or the player. Even from Video mode or an album row showing the music video, an individual download saves the song's audio and shows its green check across the app. Accounts without a stock Download menu item get one too. A failed download says why.
- **No Playlist:** Individually downloaded songs that belong to no downloaded playlist or album appear together as
  No Playlist, not as loose songs in Downloads. It opens our own full-screen song list with right-side green checks
  and plays in the shown order from the song you tap, online and offline. Online, rows before the tapped song follow
  the end of the list, ahead of radio. Playback uses saved audio while keeping online lyrics and radio.
- **Full song menus:** The three-dot menu and long press on a No Playlist song open Music's full native menu for that exact song, with the available Share, album, playlist, queue and other stock actions. Opening another song's menu does not change the current playback or queue. The complete menu is saved for offline use; older copies need their No Playlist page opened online once to obtain it.
- **Remove download:** The Download item in a saved song's menu, including the player's three-dot menu, becomes
  Remove download with confirmation. The header button of a fully downloaded playlist or album does the same.
  Copies still needed by another downloaded list or an individual download are kept. Download and Remove download
  are not duplicated beside Music's own newer menu rows.
- **Library refresh and restart:** Downloads refreshes its rows and No Playlist count after downloads or removals, including when returning with Back. Restarting the app returns the Library tab to the Library, not the Downloads chip, with working back navigation. Device files uses Music's own device-files library and keeps existing stream copies.
- **Interrupted lists:** An interrupted playlist or album download no longer leaves its tracks in No Playlist or counts as complete. Its Download button finishes the job; the green check and Remove download appear when all available tracks are saved.
- **Android Auto:** Downloaded Playlists includes No Playlist, with artwork. Starting a downloaded track no longer crashes or stalls after an online session. Online playback keeps lyrics and radio while using the local copy. The songs after the tapped No Playlist song are inserted together, in order, before radio. Next, Previous, rapid changes of selection and reconnection no longer let an older request replace the current queue. Menu lookups do not change that queue.

## Features

### YouTube
- **Sync with anddea/revanced-patches dev:** The changes up to v4.4.0-dev.6 are merged into this fork.
- **Glass navigation bar spacing:** A bottom spacing slider in the Glass navigation bar size dialog sets how far the capsule floats above the bottom of the screen, and snackbars show right above the navigation bar.
- **Navigation bar fixes:** With Translucent or Transparent style, or Glass navigation bar, the feed draws behind the system buttons without an empty black or white strip below it. The buttons no longer sit too high with gesture navigation, including when Glass is off. The glass capsule follows Morphe's placement. The blurred background of the Translucent bar and of Glass is drawn only on Android 14 and newer; on Android 12 and 13 the bar keeps a plain translucent color because the blur could crash the app while the player moves.
- **Feed cards:** With some accounts the cards had black gutters on both sides of the thumbnails, square corners, a small look, and an inline preview broke the cards around it. Margins and corners now follow the screen density, also after it changes, and grid cards such as channel pages are clipped in their own columns. Dynamic colors tint the whole card below the thumbnail on these accounts too. Playlists, mixes and podcasts in the feed and channel home follow the Classic layout or card background like videos, and keep their layout while the app updates its templates.
- **Unlock queue:** With Unlock queue on, "Play next in queue" in the feed menu uses YouTube's own queue. "Add to RVX queue" still opens the RVX queue dialog. Turn Unlock queue off to override the feed queue button. Premium-style queue takes priority when enabled.
- **About screen:** The About card moved into an About screen at the end of RVX settings.
- **Download option icons:** "Show download option icons", off by default, shows icons beside Include subtitles and Include SponsorBlock in the built-in downloader.
- **Feature flags manager:** RVX settings > Miscellaneous > Debugging has a Feature flags manager, with Binary search to find which YouTube feature flag causes a problem. If the app fails to start twice in a row while flag overrides or a binary search are active, the third start resets them and tells you so.
- **Toolbar:** The Create button opens the upload menu again.
- **Watch later improvements:** Options to widen the drag handles of Watch later videos and hide the snackbar shown after removing a video.
- **Post buttons:** A Post buttons screen hides the like, share and comment buttons of posts, with an option to give every post the same grouped button layout.
- **Captions:** Captions show in stable blocks and as two languages at once, on YouTube 21.15 and newer.
- **Spoof video streams:** Video streams are fetched sooner so videos start faster, and inline feed previews stay muted.

### YouTube Music
- **Lyrics:** A dynamic lyrics background and the reading of each Japanese word above the text (furigana).
- **Stream download:** The default Download method saves private stream copies inside the app, separately from device-file downloads. Radio, lyrics and the queue stay online while a connection is available; playback uses the local copy. Without internet the copies still play, including with Spoof video streams enabled. The Stream downloads action shows their size and can delete them without touching device files. Individual songs save audio; playlist and album downloads keep the saved-video behavior described below.
- **Green checks:** A green check at the right end of a song row, next to its menu or drag handle, means a stream copy exists. It appears on playlist pages, album tracks, the Search songs filter and the player queue, and on a playlist or album Download button when every available track has a copy. Album rows also mark individually downloaded songs when the album itself was never downloaded. Device-file-only downloads are not marked. Checks are enabled by default.
- **Audio first:** Downloaded songs start in Song mode by default, including from album tracks, Play and Next. For a song without a saved video, the Song/Video switch still reaches the online video and keeps the playback position in both directions, unless the position is unknown or within 3 seconds of the end.
- **Video copy:** Downloading an album also saves the 360p video of songs with a matched music video, paired with audio at the selected Download quality; size depends on the source. Matching uses the title or a similar length; uncertain matches save no video. A playlist whose tracks are not linked to music videos saves audio only, and an individual song download saves no video. A video that cannot be saved does not fail the song or list. Completion messages and Stream downloads count video copies and their size; removing the stream copies removes their videos too.
- **Song and Video mode from the saved video:** A song with a saved video uses the saved 360p video and its selected-quality audio pair in both modes, online and offline. Music's own Song/Video switch flips in place without reloading, interrupting audio or changing position. Song mode uses the saved pair's audio track. Tapping a song in an album, playlist or Downloads starts that song, and Next and the end of a song continue in the chosen mode. Songs without a saved video keep their audio copy. Seeking works in Video mode offline too.
- **Offline cover and video:** Song mode shows the album cover offline. Play one saved video online after installing this version so the app can keep the player settings needed for offline video.
- **Offline album taps:** Tapping an album track offline plays that track, not the album's first track.
- **Offline replay:** Each copy keeps its song details for offline title and cover display. Earlier copies fill in these details while online. Open downloaded songs shows how many are offline ready.
- **No connection sheet:** The offline "No connection" sheet no longer covers the controls while a downloaded song plays.
- **Unavailable tracks:** Deleted, private or blocked tracks no longer fail a whole playlist or album download. Available tracks are downloaded and the completion message says how many were skipped. A failure names its reason in one line.
- **Downloads inside the Library:** Downloads is a chip filter inside the Library, with Songs, Playlists and Albums filters, online and offline. Individually saved songs are grouped as No Playlist. After restarting, the Library tab opens the Library rather than restoring Downloads.
- **Offline playlist and album pages:** Opening a downloaded playlist or album online records Music's native page, about 90 KB per playlist or 22 KB per album. It then opens offline with its header, cover, rows and checks, including from the Albums chip. Tapping a track plays its copy and continues through the list.
- **Online or offline at the tap:** A Downloads row uses the connection state when tapped, not when drawn, avoiding a stale redownload prompt. Online, a playlist or album opens its normal page.
- **Android Auto:** Stream copies appear with artwork inside Downloaded Playlists independently of Device files. No Playlist is included. Playback uses local audio, retaining online features while connected and working after an online session or a fully offline cold start.

## Compatibility and verification

Supported patching versions:
- YouTube: **21.39.525, 21.13.164, 20.05.46**.
- YouTube Music: **9.40.51, 9.15.51, 8.30.54**.

The YouTube Music changes were exercised on the rooted Moto Edge Plus 2023 with Music 9.40.51. Android Auto was tested through the Desktop Head Unit: online first and middle selections, ordered Next and Previous, radio after the saved list, repeated and rapid selections, reconnection, offline playback after an online session, and a fully offline cold start. Native No Playlist menus were tested for the tapped song while another song played, including Share, album, playlist picker, Play next, long press and Remove download, without changing the playing queue merely by opening a menu.

On the test account, High saved Opus 251, Normal AAC 140 (128,331 bps), Low HE-AAC 139 (48,492 bps), and Highest
saved Opus 251 because 141/774 were not offered. Live Premium 141/774 availability and measured zero audible
interruption using PCM capture were not verified. The 360p test pair used video 134 and AAC 140.

Not verified: YouTube 21.13.164 and 20.05.46 and YouTube Music 9.15.51 and 8.30.54 at runtime; the navigation bar fixes on Android 15 and newer, HyperOS gesture navigation or the Opaque style; the end of Feature flags manager Binary search (unit-tested only); light theme on the test phone; YouTube offline library serving after the Spoof video streams change; the reporter's feed-card layout on an affected account; playlists whose songs the server links to music videos; auto-advance at the end of a song in Video mode; Previous in Video mode offline; an offline restored player; or Android Auto on a physical car head unit.

Known behavior:
- A playlist or album page is recorded only when opened online. Until then, offline playback starts from its first downloaded song.
- Covers never seen online show as grey squares offline; only Music's image cache is used.
- A Downloads view built online and tapped immediately after the network drops can show a spinner for about 6 seconds before the page appears.
- Older individual copies need No Playlist opened online once to save their full native menus for offline use.
- The module builder's existing YouTube light-theme background option is ignored: the Theme patch does not expose `lightThemeBackgroundColor`. Both tested CLI versions warn about that option; patching otherwise completes.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/lavinhoque33/revanced-patches/compare/v1.34.0-dev.6...v1.34.0-dev.7)
